about_company.about_short: World's leading provider of customized cryogenic equipment
about_company.about_long: INOX India (INOXCVA) describes itself as a leading global provider of customized cryogenic equipment, with over 30 years of experience in design, manufacturing and installation. It makes cryogenic storage tanks, transport tanks and systems for industrial gases (oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen), LNG infrastructure, and advanced scientific applications (fusion, aerospace), plus stainless-steel beverage kegs. Its decks cite 5,000+ customers across 100+ countries over its history; the FY26 annual report says it served 590+ customers in FY26, across industrial gas, energy, healthcare, aerospace and food & beverage end-markets. Revenue comes from the sale of equipment and turnkey project solutions, and exports were about 59% of FY26 consolidated revenue.
about_company.business_intro: INOX India (INOXCVA) designs and builds cryogenic tanks, trailers and systems that store and move industrial gases and LNG, engineered equipment for science and space projects such as the ITER fusion reactor, and stainless-steel beer kegs. It sells to industrial gas producers, LNG operators, research institutions and breweries, and earns revenue on each equipment order or turnkey project; about 59% of FY26 revenue came from exports.

company_timeline.title: Founded as INOXCVA by Pavan Kumar Jain
company_timeline.detail: Set up to make India self-reliant in cryogenic tanks and solutions. The FY26 annual report dates the company's inception to 1991.

business_facts.title: Top 10 customers are 51% of revenue
business_facts.text: The top ten customers contributed 51% of FY26 revenues, up from about 47% of revenue from operations in FY25 and 45.7% in FY24. The largest single customer was about 13% in FY25 and 8.5% in FY24. The company served 590+ customers in FY26; its decks cite 5,000+ customers across 100+ countries over its history.

business_facts.title: Exports rose from 34% to about 59% of revenue
business_facts.text: Exports were 34% of total income in FY22, 45% in FY23 and 55% in FY24, around 53% in FY25 and approximately 59% of total income in FY26. Key export geographies are the US, Europe, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Korea, UAE, Australia and Bangladesh.

business_facts.title: Four manufacturing locations in India, plus Brazil and Europe
business_facts.text: Large-scale serial manufacturing at four locations in India, part manufacturing and service distribution from one location in Brazil, and a stock-and-sale facility in the Netherlands. Export-oriented manufacturing sits in the Kandla Special Economic Zone.

business_facts.title: Order backlog of ₹1,514 Cr at end-FY26, 63% export
business_facts.text: Order backlog stood at ₹1,514 Cr at the end of FY26: 49% industrial gas, 28% LNG, 22% Cryo Scientific Division and 1% others including kegs. Export orders were 63% of the backlog. Order inflow in FY26 was ₹1,685 Cr, up 9.9%.

sources.label: INOX India Annual Report 2025-26

business_facts.title: Keg plant capacity of about 300,000 kegs a year
business_facts.text: Installed keg capacity is around 300,000 kegs a year; FY26 sales were around 61,000 kegs, up from 46,000 in FY25, and management said the plant ran at about one-third of capacity. Keg revenue was about ₹26.13 Cr in FY26 against ₹27.15 Cr in FY25 as the mix moved to smaller kegs. Heineken, AB InBev and Molson Coors have approved its kegs.

business_facts.title: 450+ engineers; mini-LNG terminals and LNG trailers
business_facts.text: An in-house team of 450+ engineers develops new products and customised solutions. The company has delivered mini-LNG terminal projects in Scotland and Antigua, with The Bahamas under execution, and more than 250 of its LNG semi-trailers operate on Indian roads (May 2026).

what_changed.headline: Industrial gas fell from 77% to 54% of revenue as LNG and cryo-scientific work scaled
what_changed.text: Consolidated revenue roughly doubled from ₹803 Cr in FY22 to ₹1,632 Cr in FY26. Industrial gas grew more slowly (₹620 Cr to ₹874 Cr) than LNG (₹126 Cr to ₹457 Cr) and the Cryo Scientific Division (₹36 Cr to ₹228 Cr), so its share fell from 77% to 54%. Over the same years exports rose from 34% of total income to about 59%.
